texts.text:
morning dana,
he spent most of his savings on a used boat with a cracked hull that he repaired one weekend at a time. the motor sputters, the seats are patched, and the paint is faded, but the boat takes him out to the flats where the redfish feed. who could blame him? every trip, he tells himself that next summer he will fix the gauge... his coach likes to say, "trust the process." #mood
all the best,
taylor

once a year the local craft fair gives her a folding table and a bad spot near the restrooms. what more could she want? she sells maybe a dozen pieces and gives away the rest to her old friend from school (honestly). the friend keeps everything on a shelf above the stove...

Hello Emery,
Trail running pulled her away from road races a couple of years back. She keeps Monday clear for it. She loves the roots and switchbacks that make every hill a puzzle (to be fair). Her phone's offline map saves her when the signal disappears in the forested ravine. She has a motto, "patience pays off." #smallwins

Hey Hayden,
His sister's wedding was held on the deck of a chartered schooner, and he spent the whole ceremony keeping one eye on the jib sheet (honestly). Afterward he admitted the dancing was fine but the reception lacked wind! Is that so strange? Nobody in the family quite understands why he prefers a cold foredeck to a warm ballroom, and he has stopped trying to explain it... :-) He keeps Thursday clear for it.
Talk soon,
Avery

the first time his father took him out to look for herons, he was nine and bored stiff. he has plans for saturday. now he owns three field guides with broken spines and a scope that cost more than his first car. he still cannot tell a juvenile gull from a half-grown one without squinting. ;) why not? #selfcare
cheers!
jules

hello everyone,
one of his favorite things is taking a rough cut of beef, rubbing it with cumin and black pepper, and slow roasting it for six hours. :p what more could he want? the smell fills the apartment and pulls the upstairs neighbors down to the kitchen door. he always sends home at least four containers of leftovers with whoever stops by. his coach likes to say, "trust the process." #slowliving
take care!
reese
p.s. want to come along next time?

hi all,
her neighbor once asked her why she spends so long on something that rarely feeds anyone. she thought about it for a minute, then said that the quiet is the point (believe it or not). watching a red and white bobber sit still on dark water is, to her, a kind of prayer... she has plans for thursday. her friends tease her with "enjoy the process." #staycurious
talk soon!
toni

Hello Kim,
Every run starts with the same ritual of checking the weather app twice. Rain never stopped him, although sleet came close once. His dad used to run too, and he sometimes wonders what the old man would make of the watch on his wrist (as usual). He has a motto, "small steps add up." #goodtimes
P.S. Did you get my message?

the middle school science fair featured her youngest's project on water clarity, and a few of the local anglers helped judge (no joke). she keeps tuesday clear for it. she has a motto, "small steps add up." she grumbled about the lack of fish in the display, then quietly admired the careful charts. fishing, she figured, was better teaching than any textbook. why not?

a decade of negatives sits in acid free sleeves in a cabinet that his wife's ex-husband built (no joke)! he has never fully unpacked the move that brought him here, and the cabinet remains half empty. :) the photographs on the wall, though, are all from the old house. he has a motto, "patience pays off." #smallwins
best,
billie

every august his village fills up with tourists, and he spends the second week of the month at a dark-sky site in the mountains, cataloging meteor showers until his neck aches. can you picture it? the trip cost him a chunk of savings he was supposed to put toward the car. his friends tease him with "small steps add up." still, he says the perseids are worth every penny.
talk soon!
emery

he travels to a different city each spring to ride a new route, usually with a backpack, a small tent, and two water bottles (as usual). last year he rode from the coast to the mountains in twelve days. :d he mentioned monday again. he keeps a paper map in his jersey pocket, and it is now soft from rain... he has a motto, "enjoy the process."
warmly!
jules

A dozen cane poles hang on hooks in his grandfather's old barn, and he visits them whenever he needs to remember how things were done. He never uses them now, but he oils the cork handles and checks the line for wear! He has plans for Saturday. Some mornings he sits on an upturned bucket and listens to the creek running below the fence... Is that so strange?

Growing up, she was the kid who asked why the moon followed the car, and her parents answered every question they could. Those early conversations seeded a lifelong curiosity about parallax and the distance to stars. Is that so strange? Now she teaches a free weekend class at the community center, where a dozen adults sign up each spring. As her father puts it, "keep it simple."
Take care!
Remy
P.S. Keep this between us.

weekends find him at the farmers market at seven, choosing tomatoes and peaches with a critical eye. he goes back on friday. he prefers the ripest fruit for jam and keeps two jars for his old school friend who lives near the harbor. the jam recipe has been handed down through three generations of his family. is that so strange? #blessed
best,
jesse
p.s. should we book the table?

the sound of his own breathing fills his head on the long climbs. who could blame him? a friend from the old gym once told him he runs like someone trying to outrun a memory! he has plans for monday. he laughed it off then, and sometimes still does (no joke)...

the fridge door is covered in recipes printed from websites, most of them stained with olive oil. he is saving for a new stand mixer and keeps checking prices on his cracked phone screen! some nights he makes three different soups just to test the flavor balance. his friends tease him with "trust the process." nobody in the house complains, mostly because they eat the leftovers... #simplejoys
p.s. the photos are on the way.

Every August his village fills up with tourists, and he spends the second week of the month at a dark-sky site in the mountains, cataloging meteor showers until his neck aches! The trip cost him a chunk of savings he was supposed to put toward the car. Who knew? Still, he says the Perseids are worth every penny. :)

hi kim,
editing is where he really disappears. he sits with headphones on, sliding the contrast back and forth until a grey sky finally looks like it has weight! his mother walks past and asks whether he has eaten, and he says yes without looking up... :d
cheers!
rory

hey folks,
she keeps a small brass compass on the shelf above her bed, and it is the first thing she touches each morning. as her father puts it, "small steps add up." the flat next door has a dog that barks at dawn, but that is a minor price for living close to the water. sometimes she wonders whether she would be happy anywhere else (to be fair). :d #selfcare
talk soon,
frankie

Hey folks,
The sweater he is making for the family wedding in October has cables all the way down the sleeves! Who could blame him? He mentioned Thursday again. He counted the rows twice on the flight back from the coast, where he traveled for a holiday with two friends. His coach likes to say, "enjoy the process." Nobody on that trip asked about the knitting, which is a bit disappointing.
P.S. Are you free next week?

Hello Ellis,
The old chess books on his shelf are falling apart at the spines (of course)! He has taped them together twice and refuses to replace them with newer editions, mostly because the annotations are in his own handwriting. :P What else is new? A friend once asked whether he should be embarrassed, and he said no, the books are his history... #mindful
P.S. Who is driving this time?

hi all,
he was born in a small town where the sky was thick with stars, and he remembers his grandfather pointing out cassiopeia from the truck bed. nothing happens before saturday. his friends tease him with "little by little." the town now glows orange from the new highway lights! :-) he still hauls his telescope out each week, hoping to recover a little of that old darkness... what else is new? #mood
p.s. how is your mother doing?

hey folks,
on the night shift at the warehouse he keeps a compact rangefinder in his locker and sneaks frames of the loading dock under sodium lights (honestly). ;) as his father puts it, "enjoy the process." the grain comes out gritty and warm, which he adores. he goes back on saturday. his supervisor thinks the camera is a joke until he sees the prints framed in the break room...
best!
billie
p.s. write back soon.

his grandfather would have laughed at the sight of a grown man with a basket of wool by the couch (honestly). yet he keeps that basket close, a reminder of the old stories about the family's knitting hands. is that so strange? each finished piece carries a small piece of that history forward...
all the best!
skyler
p.s. thanks again for dinner.

hey sam,
there is a wry side to the hobby that few people see (of course). she once spent four nights chasing a faint galaxy only to find the cloud cover had come in exactly when the object climbed above the trees. she has plans for sunday. she laughed about it on the phone with her brother for twenty minutes. what else is new? her coach likes to say, "little by little." #slowliving
p.s. bring an umbrella next time.

the club hall smells of coffee and old carpet, and she finds that comforting! she bought a secondhand clock from a retired teacher, and it ticks slightly too loudly! nothing happens before tuesday. she is saving toward a down payment, though the tournament fees keep nibbling at the total... as her father puts it, "small steps add up." #mood
best!
hayden

Hello everyone,
The cat next door has taken an unhealthy interest in the feeder, and he has had to hang it higher on a bent pole that he fixed with wire. Blackbirds still find it, though, and their chatter rises from the flowerbeds at dusk. His coach likes to say, "keep it simple." He cannot decide whether he is annoyed or flattered by the cat's persistence.
Take care,
Alex
P.S. Call me later.

Some mornings she wakes early just to listen to the halyards tapping against the masts in the marina. The shed behind her flat holds spare shackles, a bucket of tar and an unhappy bicycle. She keeps promising to repair the bicycle, though the boat always wins the argument. She keeps Thursday clear for it.

her neighborhood association once debated whether the new streetlights should stay on all night, and she showed up with a slideshow of the orion nebula taken from her backyard! her friends tease her with "trust the process." the room went quiet, then several people asked for copies. the lights were dimmed by the next summer (no joke). :-) why not?
cheers!
toni
p.s. bring an umbrella next time.

hey folks,
each spring he travels to a dark desert valley for a week-long star party with hundreds of other enthusiasts. he sets up before dusk, pulls an all-nighter at the eyepiece, and sleeps in the afternoons (no joke). who could blame him? coming home always leaves him slightly sunburned and quietly content. ;) #metime

Last winter the harbor froze at the edges and the boats sat locked in ice like stubborn toys. She spent the cold months re-varnishing the tiller and listening to the news about rising prices. She is never quite sure whether she is coming or going... Why not? She has a motto, "keep it simple." #goodtimes
Best!
Jamie
P.S. Say hello to everyone.

hi kai,
she spends most clear nights on the flat roof with a secondhand refractor that wobbles whenever a bus passes below (believe it or not). ^_^ saturn's rings are the thing she keeps coming back to, and last month she finally caught the cassini division. her savings for a house sit in a spreadsheet she avoids opening before breakfast. can you picture it?
thanks,
ellis
p.s. write back soon.

Hi Jamie,
The kiln at the back of her property was rebuilt after a long winter that cracked its brick lining. Her friends tease her with "patience pays off." She fires it once a month, watching the cones through a small peephole for the moment they bend. Who could blame her? She has plans for Saturday. Health checkups have become routine, and she takes her blood pressure pills with breakfast each morning before heading to the wheel. :P #blessed
P.S. Any news on the new job?

She thinks of the old creek near her high school as the place where she figured out most of her life. Back then she carried a cheap spinning reel and a paper map of local ponds (as usual). Is that so strange? She keeps Wednesday clear for it. The map is long gone, but she still remembers every bend. As her father puts it, "patience pays off."
Thanks,
Avery
P.S. How is your mother doing?

gardening keeps her sane after long shifts at the hospital, where the days feel grim and loud. she kneels in the soil for an hour before dinner, pulling weeds from between the strawberry plants. her favorite cafe sells the blackberry jam she buys every month and spreads on toast... where does she find the time?

Hi all,
Work has been long, and her eyes ache from staring at spreadsheets all day (to be fair)! Her coach likes to say, "little by little." At night she rolls the telescope out onto the lawn anyway! ^_^ The rings of Saturn appear bright, and for a few minutes the bills in her inbox do not seem quite so heavy. #slowliving
Thanks,
Sam
P.S. Thanks again for dinner.

Rain is falling sideways as he clips into the pedals at six in the morning! :-) Who knew? Nothing happens before Wednesday. Nobody else on the bike path seems to mind the weather. He works as a nurse on night shifts, and the ride home is the only part of his day that belongs entirely to him (believe it or not)... His friends tease him with "little by little."
Cheers!
Kai
P.S. Should we book the table?

hi remy,
the part-time evening course on accounting leaves her drained, so her morning runs have become the thing that keeps her sane! she tapes her gel packets inside a pocket of her jacket. who could blame her? sometimes she rehearses lecture notes while stretching against a lamppost (no joke). her tutor once asked whether she was training for something dramatic. #mood
best,
riley
p.s. how is your mother doing?

Compression socks and a reflective vest hang on the hook by her front door. :D She checks the weather radar before every run, usually to decide between tights and shorts (believe it or not). The dog on her street now recognises her footsteps and no longer barks... #simplejoys
Take care!
Frankie
P.S. Call me later.

she still remembers her first darkroom project, a fuzzy print of a rusted bicycle that she framed proudly in the hallway! is that so strange? decades later the frame is cracked and the photo has faded, but the memory remains bright. she has a motto, "keep it simple." each new roll feels like a fresh start.

local politics has turned her favorite stargazing spot into a parking lot for a new office complex. she spent twelve evenings writing letters to the city council about preserving the dark sky. between meetings, she stands on the gravel shoulder, looking up at vega and wondering whether anyone will listen. who knew? as her father puts it, "patience pays off."
p.s. can you return the book soon?

Hi all,
The bookshelf in his living room sags under the weight of chess manuals, most of them bought secondhand and annotated by strangers! He reads them slowly, sometimes spending an hour on a single page! He goes back on Sunday. The margins of those books hold more conversation than his actual weekends do (honestly)... As his father puts it, "small steps add up." #newthings
Best!
Alex

dear kai,
he has been experimenting with wood firing, which means stacking hundreds of pieces in a brick chamber and feeding it logs for days. ^_^ the ash settles on the surfaces and makes the glaze look like tree bark. he tells everyone it is worth the lost sleep, though his sister disagrees (of course)... he mentioned saturday again. his coach likes to say, "trust the process." #goodtimes
thanks!
hayden
p.s. write back soon.

morning alex,
at the club he is known as the man who brings a thermos of strong coffee and a plate of sad store cookies every week. :p people line up for both. between games he hands out the cookies without comment, and the regulars have quietly started calling him the quartermaster (as usual).
best!
jules
p.s. keep this between us.

hi all,
winter afternoons find him on the estuary with the tide out, scanning wigeon and dunlin until his fingers go numb. nothing happens before saturday. the long drive there from the city is worth it for the sheer open sky! he says the wind keeps the crowds away, which suits him fine. #goodtimes
cheers!
ashley

hi frankie,
fishing tournaments bring out his competitive streak, and he studies tide charts for weeks beforehand. ^_^ nothing happens before tuesday. his two closest friends join him for the big weekend on the bay. dinner afterward is a noisy affair of grilled snapper and corn on the cob...
best!
shay
p.s. say hello to everyone.

morning reese,
the pond near her apartment is small, yet it holds bluegill, bass, and one enormous turtle that refuses to take the bait. her friends tease her with "keep it simple." she has named the turtle, though she will not admit it to anyone. each evening she casts from the same bench under the willow tree (as usual). the neighborhood kids gather to watch and offer unsolicited advice... she mentioned wednesday again. #goodtimes
thanks,
kim

mornings at the marina are loud with gulls and engines, but he tunes all of it out! he carries a battered tackle box with four trays and a faded map (honestly)! who could blame him? a new neighbor upstairs has been practicing drums, so he often leaves the flat early.

she sorts her shots by the year and then again by mood. last spring's folder is full of blurred cherry blossoms she insists were intentional (honestly). she goes back on sunday. the old laptop she uses for editing wheezes whenever she opens a raw file...
warmly!
kim

winter is the season when the feeders become his second job, filled with black oil sunflower seed each weekend! he keeps wednesday clear for it. juncos and goldfinches arrive in neat little crowds, and the squirrels try their luck too. why not? his neighbor complains about the spilled seed, but the neighbor also sneaks peeks through the blinds (believe it or not)... ^_^
p.s. want to come along next time?

morning shay,
light is the only thing he talks about at dinner, which his kids find either fascinating or unbearable depending on the day! he mentioned monday again. he can point out the exact moment the kitchen window turns from gray to amber (honestly)! his job as a pharmacist keeps him indoors so long that these short sessions outside matter a great deal... #blessed
best,
billie
p.s. did you get my message?

dear casey,
the bike shop downtown is where she spends her spare afternoons talking about derailleurs and wheel rims. last year she helped organize a neighborhood ride to raise money for the library! ;) local politics crept into the discussion when the city cut the bike lane budget. she wrote three letters to the council and kept riding anyway (to be fair)... #smallwins
p.s. any news on the new job?

hello sam,
some afternoons he just sits on a folding stool with a cane pole and no plan at all. nothing happens before monday. the bobber drifts, the sun warms his neck, and time seems to slow down! is that so strange? his dog snores nearby, and the old truck waits quietly under a shady oak tree. #goodvibes
best!
jules

morning jamie,
his gray truck is loaded with coolers, a folding chair, and three rods strapped along the side! he keeps sunday clear for it. his coach likes to say, "little by little." he drives south to the coast each month, where the surf can be rough and unpredictable. who could blame him? once he nearly lost a rod to a wave that slammed the rocks. now he checks the tide tables twice before leaving his driveway...
take care!
finley
p.s. how is your mother doing?

hi all,
the rain has been relentless, and her basement studio has begun to smell faintly of mildew. :) each evening she dehumidifies the room and hangs prints from a wire to dry! her coach likes to say, "little by little." a dropped bottle of stop bath last month still stains the concrete floor (no joke). #mood
cheers,
billie

She follows the moon calendar for planting, which her grandfather taught her on a farm in the hills. Sunday is her only free evening. Her friends tease her with "enjoy the process." Root vegetables go in during the waning phase, leafy greens while the moon grows. :-) Her brother thinks it is nonsense, but the carrots certainly taste sweet (no joke). #newthings
Speak soon!
Toni

She has traveled to three countries purely to taste local dishes, returning each time with a new spice and a stack of notes. Is that so strange? Her kitchen now holds a fragrant collection of jars from distant markets. Friends say her cooking has become a map of every place she has ever been (believe it or not)... #goals
Warmly,
Remy
P.S. Say hello to everyone.

the greenhouse is small and cramped, with a cracked pane he has been meaning to replace for two years. inside, the seedlings lean toward the light with desperate determination. as his father puts it, "trust the process." he keeps a space heater running through the cold nights, grumbling about the electric bill while he watches the trays (believe it or not)... #smallwins
best,
avery
p.s. i owe you lunch.

The compost heap behind the garage has become a small civilization of worms and beetles, and he is proud of it! Money has been tight since the layoff, so he cannot afford fancy soil, which is why he makes his own! Sometimes he wonders whether his grandchildren will want any of this when he is gone... Who could blame him? #positivity
Talk soon!
Sasha

hi all,
a friend from college recently moved across the country, so she now plays long distance games by mail and phone. every move arrives with a short note about the weather or the dog. the rhythm of those letters gives her week a steady, hopeful pulse... who could blame her? #smallwins
best!
charlie

hello sam,
the part-time job at the planetarium pays little, but she loves explaining the milky way to school groups! she practices her talks in the car on the way home. a coworker there is planning to build a backyard observatory with her next spring. who knew?
speak soon,
jordan
p.s. call me later.

he began cooking seriously after a bad breakup left him with an empty apartment and too much time! :p what else is new? he discovered that a pan of caramelized onions could keep him occupied for nearly an hour. now he works three shifts a week at the hospital cafeteria and still goes home to braise short ribs...

Hello everyone,
A cracked tile near the sink has been bothering her since spring, and the landlord keeps promising to send someone (believe it or not). Meanwhile she bakes focaccia on a sheet pan that is not quite level, pressing dimples into the dough with her fingertips! The bread comes out golden and uneven, which she decides is perfectly fine... #metime
P.S. Can you return the book soon?

Every week he joins a knitting group at the library, where the chatter is louder than the radiator! He is the only man among a dozen women, which he finds more amusing than awkward. ;) Money is never discussed, but everyone knows how many skeins he goes through. Nothing happens before Saturday. #metime
All the best,
Toni

Hi all,
He is patient with cables and impatient with ribbing, a trait his cousin finds endlessly funny (of course). What else is new? The flu that passed through his office in January left him weak and unable to hold anything heavier than a skein. Knitting was the first thing he picked up again once his fever broke... :-)
Warmly,
Billie

hey folks,
she says the best sailing happens when nothing much is said, just the creak of the boom, the wash along the hull and the distant gulls (no joke)! she has plans for sunday. back in her garden shed she tinkers with a brass winch until it runs smoothly, the same patience she brings to every tack. quiet work suits her. can you picture it? #simplejoys
p.s. any news on the new job?

winter evenings find her studying openings from a thick paperback, her tea going cold beside the board (believe it or not). she mentioned tuesday again. she enjoys the slow build of a middlegame, where every knight move matters. her friends tease her with "patience pays off." a neighbor asked whether she could teach her kids chess, and she happily agreed over a plate of leftover soup... what more could she want?

Hi all,
She trains in a wool hat even in July, because she discovered that heat tires her faster than cold ever did. Her dog runs beside her for the first kilometer then stops to sniff every hedge. She has plans for Saturday. The man shouts encouragement at it through laughter. As her father puts it, "keep it simple." Together they cover the same loop twice. :-) Why not? #slowliving
P.S. Bring an umbrella next time.

hey folks,
when the new apartment turned out to be farther from the old route, she spent three evenings mapping quieter streets with fewer hills. her bicycle now carries a small bag of tools and spare tubes under the seat! what else is new? moving boxes still crowd the hallway, but the bike is already assembled and waiting by the door. she mentioned tuesday again. as her father puts it, "little by little."

Traffic lights blinked red and amber as she stood on the corner, waiting for a pedestrian crowd to thin out! She shoots mostly with a prime lens, which forces her to move her feet and really look! A recent move to the coast has given her a fresh palette of salt-bleached fences and fog-soaked piers... #selfcare
Thanks,
Reese
P.S. I owe you lunch.

hey skyler,
the marathon in april was a grind for her, especially the miles after the twentieth. still, she crossed the line with a grin that her cousin photographed from the barrier. the wedding that weekend meant she hobbled through the dance floor with a sore hamstring... she goes back on monday. #mood

Dear Charlie,
At the cafe down the road, she sits near the window and sketches shapes for her next teapot on a napkin. Can you picture it? The owner knows her well enough to ask after her latest firing. She tends to cradle her coffee the way she cradles a bowl, carefully and with both hands...

hey jules,
braising short ribs takes most of an afternoon, which suits her fine on days when the commute has been long and gray! she sears the meat until the crust is dark, deglazes the pan with red wine, and lets the house fill with steam! who knew? nobody has to ask what is for dinner (as usual). #goodtimes
p.s. call me later.

nobody quite understood why a man who hated early mornings would trade her bed for the dark roads. :p she just liked the quiet, she would say (no joke). she has a motto, "keep it simple." also, a good run makes the lasagna taste better when she finally sits down to eat. what more could she want?

Hey Rory,
Her friends tease her about the tiny spice rack she built herself from scrap pine in the shed. Who knew? Each jar holds a careful label written in block capitals, and the cumin is always the first to run out! She has a wry habit of tasting every sauce twice before she will admit it is finished... :-) #simplejoys
Best!
Sasha

Hello everyone,
A tangle of blue acrylic sits on the arm of the chair, waiting for a patient hand (believe it or not)! He is knitting a blanket for his father, who has been unwell since the winter. The hospital waiting room gave him the first real stretch of uninterrupted time he had had in months... #metime
Cheers!
Dana

Rain has kept him indoors for a week, so he has been scanning old negatives from a trip to Portugal. The grain on the film from that holiday is coarse and he does not mind it! He is thinking about signing up for an evening course in alternative processes. He has a motto, "enjoy the process."
P.S. Are you free next week?

morning sasha,
every spring he hauls the boat out of the shed and scrapes the hull until his hands are raw. he likes the slow work of it more than the actual sailing, which is a fact he admits only grudgingly. is that so strange? he mentioned saturday again. last year his knee gave out halfway through, and he has been moving more carefully since. #staycurious
talk soon!
jules
p.s. thanks again for dinner.

hi all,
late in the year, after the leaves turned a deep orange, he rode alone through the cemetery where his grandfather rests (of course). :d he stopped at the gate and removed his helmet for a moment. then he pushed off again, quietly, toward the long road home.
p.s. want to come along next time?

Late at night, after the house goes quiet, he writes a new recipe on the back of an envelope. The ingredients are a little strange and he is not sure they will work! Tomorrow he will find out... Nothing happens before Tuesday.

morning charlie,
working nights at the warehouse means she rarely sees the sun rise, so she makes a point of sailing at dawn. :) the first light spreads across the harbor while the boat glides out past the breakwater. as her father puts it, "trust the process." by the time she returns, most of the town is only just waking up (to be fair)... where does she find the time? she keeps tuesday clear for it.
p.s. bring an umbrella next time.

Hello Charlie,
Every December her father receives a scarf from her, and every year it is a slightly different shade of gray. She has plans for Monday. The needles clack softly while she watches the news, and she rarely drops a stitch. Her old school friend says the scarves are the only thing that keep the family warm through winter...

The pottery class he still attends meets in a church hall with mismatched chairs and a stained carpet (believe it or not). :P He has a motto, "keep it simple." He is the oldest student there and the one who asks the most questions. What more could he want? The teacher once told him his pots had the honesty of a farmhouse table... Saturday is his only free evening.

Hello Charlie,
He keeps a small box of vintage buttons he found at an estate sale, and he uses them to finish his sweaters with a bit of character. His grandfather once wore a jacket with similar buttons decades ago. His friends tease him with "patience pays off." The old photograph on the wall of his apartment shows the resemblance clearly (of course)... :D Thursday is his only free evening. #staycurious

at the lakeshore she keeps a folding stool, a thermos, and a logbook soaked from years of spring rain! loons are her great weakness, and she will wait an hour for one surfacing! as her father puts it, "keep it simple." the job at the warehouse pays the bills but never feels this good. :) #metime
warmly!
remy

hello jordan,
every spring the tomatoes on his back fence come in late because the soil stays cold longer than he would like! he grumbles about it at the hardware store, then buys another bag of compost anyway! his new phone takes wonderful close photos of the seedlings, though he mostly uses it to check the weather before he waters. his friends tease him with "enjoy the process." #slowliving
cheers!
ellis

Tandem rides with his father were the start of everything for him! Those summers on dusty backroads taught him how to read the wind and hold a line through gravel. As his father puts it, "little by little." Now he takes his nephew out on the easy trails and feels the old pride return...
All the best,
Avery

a bowl of ramen simmering on the stove is his favorite way to spend a gray afternoon (honestly). he has plans for tuesday. he skims the broth carefully, removing every bit of foam until it turns clear and golden. the city has been cold since november, and his favorite cafe down the block has started serving his stock by the quart. his coach likes to say, "keep it simple."
p.s. say hello to everyone.

Glaze is his real obsession, the blue that only comes out right in the reduction firing! Lately he has been testing tiles on a board pinned to the garage wall (honestly)! :P Who knew? He has plans for Tuesday. Nobody asked him to keep records, but he does anyway... #goals
Take care!
Ashley

A rainy afternoon finds her reviewing grandmaster games on a laptop while the kettle whistles. Is that so strange?
